channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: 54,9% acham que Tarcísio será reeleito, indica Paraná Pesquisas
item.description: A Paraná Pesquisas survey shows that 54.9% of São Paulo voters believe Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicans) will be re-elected in October 2026. In contrast, only 28.6% of respondents expect Fernando Haddad (PT) to win. Just 1.2% backed the former mayor, whose name was not specified in the excerpt.

item.title: A disputa entre Tarcísio e Haddad pelo governo de São Paulo, segundo o Paraná Pesquisas
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) leads the race for São Paulo governor with 47.3% in the first round and 52.7% in the second round, according to a Paraná Pesquisas survey released on May 21, 2026. Fernando Haddad (PT) follows with 33.5% in the first round and 37.6% in the second, while other candidates such as Paulo Serra (PSDB) and Kim Kataguiri (Missão) trail below 5%. The margin of error is 2.5 percentage points.

item.title: Efeito Master: queda de Flávio Bolsonaro deixa Lula isolado na liderança
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro experienced a 5.4 percentage point drop in the Atlas/Bloomberg poll due to the 'Master Effect', linked to his financial dealings with Daniel Vorcaro, former owner of Banco Master, who was arrested for billion-dollar financial frauds. This left Lula isolated in the lead with 47% voting intentions, stable since March. The Liberal Party challenged the poll in Electoral Court, claiming the questions were not neutral.

item.title: A irregularidade eleitoral do presidente Lula ‘esquecida’ pelo TSE
item.description: On May 1, 2024, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva committed electoral illegality by explicitly asking voters to support Guilherme Boulos, then a pre-candidate for mayor of São Paulo, during a period when pre-campaign propaganda is prohibited. The Electoral Justice initially fined Lula R$20,000 and Boulos R$15,000 for antecipated electoral propaganda, later reduced on appeal to R$15,000 and R$10,000. Although a special appeal was filed with the TSE and remains unresolved since March 2025, Lula has since repeated similar violations using official government events to solicit votes.

item.title: Agência de ex-marketeiro de Flávio Bolsonaro tem R$ 99 milhões em contratos com governo federal
item.description: The advertising agency Cálix Propaganda, owned by Marcello Lopes — former marketer for Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign — has secured R$ 99.28 million in federal government contracts from April 2022 to May 2026, originally established under Jair Bolsonaro’s administration and continued under Lula. Lopes departed Flávio Bolsonaro’s campaign following a dispute with Daniel Vorcaro, while the senator admitted to meeting banker Vorcaro after the arrest of Sérgio Lima. Key contracts, including a potential R$ 55 million/year deal with the Ministry of Integration and Regional Development, were extended via amendments during Lula’s term.

item.title: Congresso analisa nesta quinta vetos sobre doações a estados e municípios durante período eleitoral
item.description: The National Congress is reviewing presidential vetoes to the 2026 Budget Guidelines Law (LDO) on Thursday, focusing on four provisions with direct electoral impact, including allowing public donations during the election period and waiving fiscal compliance requirements for small municipalities. The Executive vetoed these measures on grounds of unconstitutionality, stating the LDO cannot override the Electoral Law or address non-budgetary matters. Overturning the vetoes requires an absolute majority in a joint session of Congress.

item.title: Cenários preocupantes
item.description: The article argues that, regardless of the outcome of the 2026 elections, Brazil's political future could face a new crossroads, especially if a frontrunner falters or a dark horse emerges. Lula, whose re-election becomes more likely as Flávio Bolsonaro's candidacy weakens, is unlikely to miss the runoff — but could lose, triggering significant instability.

item.title: 8 em cada 10 aprovam isenção do IR para quem ganha até R$ 5 mil
item.description: A Locomotiva Institute and QuestionPro survey shows 85% of Brazilians approve the income tax exemption for those earning up to R$ 5,000 monthly, a 2026 measure. This is the most recognized IR change, with 77% awareness, especially among AB classes (85%). Other reforms like faster refunds and pre-filled declarations also have strong support (78-83%), and approval of the exemption is bipartisan, with 88% of right-wing and 90% of left-wing voters in favor.

item.title: Tarcísio lidera disputa ao governo de SP com 47,3%, diz pesquisa
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas leads the São Paulo gubernatorial race with 47.3% voter intention, followed by Fernando Haddad at 33.5%, according to a Paraná Pesquisas survey conducted May 18–20, 2026. In a potential runoff, Tarcísio would win with 52.7% against Haddad’s 37.6%, while Haddad faces higher rejection (44.9%) than Tarcísio (27.3%).

item.title: 64,4% aprovam e 31,5% desaprovam Tarcísio em São Paulo, diz pesquisa
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas of São Paulo has a 64.4% approval rating and 31.5% disapproval according to a Paraná Pesquisas survey from May 2026. His government is rated as 'excellent' or 'good' by 48.6% of voters, while 22.5% view it as 'bad' or 'terrible'. The survey interviewed 1,640 people between May 18-20, with a 2.5 percentage point margin of error and is registered with the TSE under SP-02706/2026.

item.title: O que diz o novo Paraná Pesquisas sobre a disputa entre Tarcísio e Haddad pelo governo de SP
item.description: According to the Paraná Pesquisas poll, Tarcísio de Freitas leads the race for São Paulo governor with 47.3% in the first round, while Fernando Haddad has 33.5%. In a potential runoff, Tarcísio would win with 52.7% against Haddad's 37.6%. Haddad is the most rejected candidate (44.9%), followed by Tarcísio (27.3%).

item.title: Hugo Souza posta vídeo com reação à ausência na lista da Copa e vibra com convocação de Neymar: ‘Eu vou estar lá’; assista
item.description: Corinthians goalkeeper Hugo Souza shared on his YouTube channel his reaction to being left out of Brazil's 2026 World Cup squad, admitting initial anxiety and sadness but celebrating the call-ups of Neymar and teammate Léo Pereira. Despite the disappointment, he emphasized his professional growth — from being unemployed two years ago to competing for a national team spot — and vowed to keep working to make the next squad, saying: 'I will be there'.

item.title: Fim da escala 6x1: entenda negociação para definir período de transição
item.description: The government is negotiating with Congress a transition rule to end the 6x1 work schedule, reducing the weekly workload from 44 to 40 hours over up to three years — two hours less in the first year and one hour in each of the next two — while paying for the non-worked hour without affecting benefits like vacation or FGTS. The proposal is a key part of Lula’s re-election campaign, framing it as a guarantee of two paid weekly rest days. The government’s main resistance remains refusing to compensate companies financially, as stated by Finance Minister Dario Durigan.

item.title: Pesquisa mostra como o impacto caso Dark Horse demora a se espalhar entre a população
item.description: A national survey conducted between May 16 and 18, following the revelation of the relationship between Flávio Bolsonaro and Daniel Vorcaro, shows that the impact of the so-called 'Dark Horse' scandal is slow to spread among the population, even with social media dissemination. Commissioned by a presidential candidate and based on 2,004 in-person voter interviews, the study indicates the scandal's news had not yet reached a broad segment of the electorate at that time. The article is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: ‘Falso profeta’ e ‘filho do diabo’: como o PT vai usar o Caso Master contra Flávio entre evangélicos
item.description: The PT is leveraging the Master Bank case to attack Senator Flávio Bolsonaro among evangelicals, labeling him a 'false prophet' and 'son of the devil' based on biblical verses. This strategy unfolds ahead of the PT's IV National Evangelical Meeting, aiming to expand the party's reach in churches nationwide despite historical evangelical resistance to Lula. The PT's Inter-religious Sector claims significant growth, with 500 thousand evangelical affiliates, and plans to use revelations about Flávio's negotiations with Daniel Vorcaro to mobilize religious leaders.

item.title: Aldo Rebelo mantém candidatura e diz que Joaquim Barbosa, ex-ministro do STF, é nome ‘clandestino’
item.description: Aldo Rebelo (DC) stated he maintains his presidential pre-candidacy and labeled Joaquim Barbosa a 'clandestine' candidate without real party support, recalling Barbosa’s 2018 withdrawal. Rebelo said he may pursue legal action if the national DC leadership, led by João Caldas, blocks his candidacy, claiming he has support from the party’s São Paulo directory. He also suggested the switch to Barbosa as candidate is tied to fears that the Master Case could affect Caldas’ family in Alagoas.

item.title: Com festas e atividades em vários bairros, conferência de música eletrônica reúne representantes de Rock in Rio, Tomorrowland e Amsterdam Dance Event no Rio
item.description: The Hot Beats Music Conference 2026, in its third edition, will gather representatives from Rock in Rio, Tomorrowland, and Amsterdam Dance Event in Rio de Janeiro from April 21 to 24 at Hotel Nacional in São Conrado. The event will feature over 100 national and international speakers, workshops, parties, and city-wide activations, covering topics such as AI, mental health, royalties, and the global expansion of Brazilian electronic music.

item.title: ‘Dark Horse’: Ancine pode aplicar multa de até R$ 100 mil contra produtora de filme de Bolsonaro
item.description: Go Up Entertainment, the producer of the film 'Dark Horse' linked to Senator Flávio Bolsonaro's 2026 presidential pre-campaign, faces a potential fine of up to R$ 100,000 from Brazil's National Cinema Agency (Ancine) for failing to report filming activities conducted in the country last year and for not providing clarifications about the production. The penalty stems from non-compliance with Brazil's Audiovisual Law, which mandates prior notification of film shoots on national territory. The issue has emerged amid the 2026 electoral pre-campaign, sparking debate over transparency and the use of public resources in politically tied cultural productions.

item.title: Perguntamos às IAs em quem votar — veja o que elas responderam, mesmo proibidas de se posicionar
item.description: BBC News Brasil tested AI models (ChatGPT, Gemini, and Grok) on electoral preferences for 2026, despite TSE bans on candidate endorsements. While ChatGPT and Gemini avoided singling out candidates, Grok showed a right-wing bias, favoring Bolsonaro and Tarcísio de Freitas and criticizing the left. Experts warn that neutrality filters can fail, even with formal restrictions in place.

item.title: Lula indica a aliados que não deve enviar nomes para agências reguladoras em meio a atritos com Alcolumbre
item.description: President Lula told allies he will not, for now, submit nominations to regulatory agencies due to heightened tensions with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre following the rejection of Attorney General Jorge Messias for the STF. While signaling readiness for a new confrontation by renominating Messias to the Supreme Court, Lula avoids negotiations with Alcolumbre, whose approval is essential for such appointments. Allies say nominations will only be sent after a direct dialogue between the two, which remains unscheduled.

item.title: Gilmar Mendes diz apoiar decretos de Lula que fiscalizam big techs
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes expressed support for Lula's decrees that hold big tech platforms accountable for criminal content, assigning oversight to the ANPD. While the rules have been in effect since 2025, they now have a dedicated regulatory body and include provisions against gender-based violence and for the protection of minors online.

item.title: A 'última dança' de Messi e Cristiano Ronaldo: Copa de 2026 deve marcar despedida de geração histórica do futebol
item.description: The 2026 World Cup is expected to mark the farewell of a historic football generation, with Lionel Messi (39) and Cristiano Ronaldo (41) likely playing their last World Cups for Argentina and Portugal, respectively. Icons such as Luka Modrić (40, Croatia) and Manuel Neuer (40, Germany) are also set to end their international careers in the tournament, symbolizing the end of an era defined by individual rivalries and records. Neymar, 34, sees the 2026 World Cup as his final opportunity to win the sport’s biggest prize with Brazil, after years of injuries and heartbreak in previous World Cups.

item.title: 'Centrão tentará se afastar de Flávio Bolsonaro se perceber que a proximidade traz mais desgaste do que ganho', diz cientista político
item.description: Political scientist Claudio Gonçalves Couto assesses that the impact of the Master case on Flávio Bolsonaro's candidacy depends on new revelations and whether he contradicts himself again. Centrão parties such as PP, Republicanos, and União Brasil tend to distance themselves from candidates who pose electoral risks, potentially remaining neutral in the first round and acting only in the second, as 'the Centrão never commits to anyone'. There is still room for Bolsonaro’s recovery if he avoids further contradictions and maintains transparency.

item.title: A menos de cinco meses da eleição, Lula acelera gastos com uma medida a cada 3,5 dias
item.description: Less than five months before the 2026 presidential elections, the Lula government has accelerated economic measures, announcing new policies on average every 3.5 days to stimulate activity and boost popularity. These initiatives—including credit expansion, subsidies, and debt renegotiation (such as Desenrola 2.0)—could impact GDP by up to 1.4 percentage points (R$ 188.7 billion), according to XP Investimentos. The government argues the effects will be gradual, peaking in Q4 as interest rate cuts transmit to credit, though concerns persist over household indebtedness and economic slowdown.

item.title: Acordão que aprovou minirreforma na Câmara torna eleição refém do sistema político
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies approved a so-called 'mini electoral reform' described as a backroom deal between Lula supporters and Bolsonaro backers, which critics argue is far from minor and instead undermines the electoral system. The reform is portrayed as a democratic setback that makes future elections hostage to entrenched political interests.

item.title: A oposição quer vencer as eleições?
item.description: The Brazilian opposition in 2026 is wasting a window of opportunity by failing to unite around a low-rejection candidate, despite empirical evidence showing most voters believe Lula does not deserve reelection. The global trend of incumbent disfavor creates favorable conditions, but internal disunity prevents the opposition from capitalizing on this discontent, particularly among Bolsonaro voters who remain strongly anti-PT. Victory requires overcoming polarization through a unified candidate, as exemplified by Peter Magyar's success in Hungary.

item.title: As perguntas sem resposta sobre a biografia de Jair Bolsonaro, 'Dark horse'
item.description: The production of the film 'Dark Horse', partially financed by Daniel Vorcaro, owner of Banco Master, is under investigation following the banker's arrest. Flávio Bolsonaro confirmed he met with Vorcaro more than once, including a meeting in late 2025, to demand payment of R$ 61 million out of the promised R$ 134 million. Federal Police are investigating whether funds sent to the Texas-based Havengate fund were used solely for the film or also to finance Eduardo Bolsonaro's stay abroad.

item.title: PL define ‘número mágico’ em pesquisa para acertar estratégia de Flávio após crise com Vorcaro
item.description: The PL commissioned a poll to assess the political impact of the crisis involving Flávio Bolsonaro and Daniel Vorcaro on the 2026 presidential race, using a 'magic number' of a ten-point Lula lead as a threshold to reconsider the senator’s candidacy viability. If the gap exceeds that, the party will discuss alternatives, including Michelle Bolsonaro as a potential replacement, though there is reluctance to the idea of Jair Bolsonaro replacing his son with his wife.

item.title: Moro defende Flávio Bolsonaro, e esquerda cobra coerência com postura na Lava-Jato
item.description: Sergio Moro defends Flávio Bolsonaro amid allegations in the Master case, drawing criticism from the left for perceived inconsistency with his Lava-Jato legacy. Opponents, including Gleisi Hoffmann and President Lula, accuse him of leniency and political manipulation of the Lava-Jato operation. Moro counters by stating he signed the Master CPI request and proposes creating a state anti-corruption agency with fixed mandates for directors.

item.title: De evangélicos ao agro, Flávio queima pontes com base fiel em meio a desgaste com filme e mudanças na equipe da campanha
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL-RJ) pre-campaign is facing wear and tear following the revelation of his closeness to Daniel Vorcaro, owner of Banco Master, which has provoked disapproval among key bolsonarist sectors: financial markets, agribusiness, and evangelical leaders. The crisis prompted the dismissal of the image consultant hired for his campaign, signaling a fracture in the senator's traditional base of support.

item.title: Silêncio de Michelle sobre Flávio é interpretado como tentativa de se manter no páreo e irrita filhos de Bolsonaro
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro's lack of public defense for Senator Flávio Bolsonaro has irritated her stepsons Carlos and Eduardo, who see her silence as a move to preserve her own political viability as a potential alternative should Flávio's candidacy weaken. Her reference to Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes as 'brother in Christ' further strained relations with hardline Bolsonarists, despite her allies denying any political calculation behind her stance.

item.title: Lisboa ganha mais 23 mil títulos e firma Portugal na ponta da eleição no exterior
item.description: Lisbon remains the largest overseas electoral college for Brazilian presidential elections, with the local consulate registering an additional 23,000 voters since 2022. The increase reflects the growing Brazilian community in Portugal and its rising participation in Brazil’s democratic process. The article is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: Baque financeiro e crise do ‘Dark Horse’ derrubaram marqueteiro de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Marcelo Lopes, known as Marcelão, requested his departure from Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL) presidential campaign in a face-to-face conversation on the night of Wednesday, the 20th, despite the campaign leadership negotiating with pollster Eduardo Fischer. The decision was made at his own initiative, ending his role in the team. The article is exclusive to subscribers.

item.title: Lula recusa tentativa de Motta de abrir canal para governo resgatar BRB
item.description: President Lula rejected the proposal to establish a direct channel with the federal government to enable a bailout of BRB, maintaining his stance against authorizing federal aid to the Brasília bank, despite pressure from Centrão leaders and Governor Celina Leão.

item.title: Saiba como foi a festa da posse de Odair Cunha como ministro do TCU
item.description: The inauguration of Minister Odair Cunha at the TCU was celebrated with a party at Fazenda Churrascada Brasília, gathering PT allies, Minas Gerais authorities, and family. The event featured a sertanejo show by Tay Gomes, a VIP area for PT leadership, and discussions about the 2026 Minas Gerais gubernatorial race, particularly focusing on Rodrigo Pacheco’s candidacy.

item.title: O vale tudo do Congresso às vésperas da eleições - O Assunto #1.724
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies approved a 'mini electoral reform' that benefits political parties by shielding public funds, limiting fines to R$30,000, allowing debt renegotiation over up to 15 years, and creating a loophole for mass automated messaging during campaigns. The bill also prevents judges from blocking or seizing funds from the Party and Electoral Funds (totaling over R$6 billion in 2026) and sets up Congress to override President Lula’s veto on campaign donations. PT, PL and the Centrão bloc voted in favor together.

item.title: Aviação bate recorde e transporta 8 milhões de passageiros em abril
item.description: Brazilian aviation transported 8,006,624 domestic passengers in April 2026, the highest monthly figure since records began in 2000. The first four months of 2026 also set records, with 33,735,228 domestic passengers and 44,309,776 total passengers (domestic and international), representing year-on-year growth of 6.5% and 7.6%, respectively. Tourism Minister Gustavo Feliciano credited the performance to Lula’s government policies, calling the sector a vital engine for the national economy, job creation, and regional development.

item.title: Cúpula do PL pouco tem a fazer
item.description: The PL leadership has little influence over Flávio Bolsonaro's candidacy, which depends solely on Jair Bolsonaro, as clarified by Valdemar Costa Neto, who stated the 15-day deadline refers to recovering polling numbers, not maintaining the candidacy. The party is attempting to mitigate fallout from negative reactions, but the political project remains under the ex-president's direct control.

item.title: Senado aprova Otto Lobo, indicado de Lula à presidência da CVM
item.description: The Senate confirmed Otto Lobo as president of the CVM (Brazilian Securities and Exchange Commission) with 31 votes in favor and 13 against, following a favorable hearing in the CAE. Lobo, who previously served as a director at the CVM under the Bolsonaro administration, will serve in an interim capacity until July 2027 after the resignation of João Pedro Nascimento. His nomination by President Lula in January sparked debate and resistance in financial markets and the Ministry of Finance due to his prior role at the agency and uncertainty over political patronage in Brasília.

item.title: Eleitores brasileiros no exterior chegam à marca de 1 milhão; número quadruplicou em 16 anos
item.description: The Brazilian electorate abroad surpassed 1 million for the first time, with 879,000 voters in regular status eligible to vote in the October elections. This represents a 308% increase compared to 2010 and exceeds the total electorate of states such as Acre, Amapá, and Roraima. The growth reflects the expanding Brazilian diaspora, which reached 5.1 million people living abroad in 2024, according to Itamaraty.

item.title: Pressão interna, crise do Master e falta de estratégia: os motivos da saída de Marcellão, marqueteiro de Flávio
item.description: Marcellão, the personal friend and campaign strategist of Flávio Bolsonaro, stepped down from the senator’s presidential pre-campaign amid internal pressure over his handling of the Master case crisis and perceived lack of communication strategy. Allies criticized the team for being overly reliant on personal trust and for reacting too slowly, leaving Bolsonaro 'trailing' the news cycle. He was replaced by publicist Eduardo Fischer, with the official explanation that he would return to the U.S. to focus on his business and family commitments.

item.title: Novo encontro entre Lula e Alcolumbre teve conversa protocolar e sem sinais de reaproximação
item.description: Lula and Alcolumbre had a brief, protocolary ten-minute meeting at the TCU without discussing controversial topics, following the Senate's rejection of Jorge Messias' STF nomination. Despite the calm interaction, allies of both say there is still no climate for a private rapprochement. Alcolumbre also missed the 100-day event of the three-powers pact against violence toward women, citing a personal commitment.

item.title: Do Polo ao Dolphin BYD: veja quais carros podem ser financiados pelo crédito para motoristas de aplicativo e taxistas
item.description: President Lula's Move Brasil program offers reduced-interest financing (12.6% annually for men, 11.5% for women) for ride-hailing drivers and taxi operators to purchase new vehicles, with a maximum loan of R$150,000. Fipe has identified 167 eligible models, including Volkswagen Virtus and Polo, Fiat Argo and Mobi, Renault Kwid, and Chevrolet Tracker, all priced within the program's limits according to Fipe and iCarros data.

item.title: Acordo entre PL e Cleitinho isola governador, e PT procura plano B para disputa em Minas
item.description: The Minas Gerais PL has drawn closer to the Republicanos party, led by Senator Cleitinho Azevedo, in a recent meeting, potentially isolating the current governor and strengthening Cleitinho’s bid for the state government. The PT, facing this development, is seeking a ‘Plan B’ for the state race, as the alliance between the two parties shifts the balance of power in the 2026 election.

item.title: Ato estudantil contra Tarcísio junta milhares e tem boneco incendiado. Veja vídeo
item.description: Student, union, and education groups held a large protest against São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicans) in the city's west zone, drawing around 30,000 participants. Demonstrators burned effigies and criticized educational materials, with tensions reported near the Palácio dos Bandeirantes as police presence intensified. The march occurred amid strikes at state universities and broader criticism of the governor's education policies.

item.title: Caso Master: PF rejeita delação de Daniel Vorcaro
item.description: The Federal Police rejected Daniel Vorcaro's plea bargain proposal, citing relevant omissions and attempts to shield influential figures in Brasília involved in the financial fraud scheme under Operation Compliance Zero. The decision was communicated to his lawyers, and as a result, Vorcaro was transferred from a special cell to a common cell at the PF Superintendence in Brasília, with lawyer access now limited to two 30-minute visits per day without work instruments.

item.title: Dirigente do DC defende 'pacificação interna' após racha por filiação de Joaquim Barbosa
item.description: Leaders of the DC (Christian Democracy) party state that the pre-candidacy of former minister Joaquim Barbosa is consolidated within the party, indicating that Aldo Rebelo will likely have to abandon his presidential bid. The party leadership advocates for 'internal pacification' following the split caused by Barbosa's affiliation, suggesting Rebelo should withdraw to prevent further divisions.

item.title: PGR se manifesta a favor de reduzir pena de homem que quebrou relógio histórico no 8 de Janeiro
item.description: The Attorney General's Office (PGR) expressed support for reducing the sentence of Antônio Cláudio Ferreira by 133 days due to his completion of high school through the ENCCEJA 2025 program. Ferreira was sentenced to 17 years in prison for his involvement in the January 8th coup attempts, during which he broke a 17th-century historical clock at the Planalto Palace. The reduction is based on Article 126, §5º, of the Penal Execution Law, which grants sentence remission for completing an educational stage.

item.title: Após crise do caso Vorcaro, coordenador de comunicação deixa campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The communications coordinator for Flávio Bolsonaro’s pre-campaign, Marcello Lopes, resigned following a scandal involving the senator and banker Daniel Vorcaro of Master. His departure came after criticism over inconsistent statements and lack of transparency regarding Bolsonaro’s relationship with Vorcaro, making his position untenable. Publicist Eduardo Fischer will take over communications leadership for the pre-campaign.

item.title: Em meio à polêmica do Master, parlamentares do PL vão ao Texas visitar Eduardo: ‘Ver nosso padrinho’
item.description: State deputies from São Paulo's PL and a councilor from Praia Grande visited Eduardo Bolsonaro in Texas, calling him their 'godfather', amid the Bolsonaro family's image crisis following Flávio Bolsonaro's negotiations with Daniel Vorcaro, former owner of Banco Master, to finance the film Dark Horse. The Federal Police is investigating whether Vorcaro's funds were diverted to a Texas-linked fund associated with Eduardo to support his stay in the U.S., though Eduardo denied receiving money from the Hevangate fund and stated his $50,000 investment in the film was early-stage and his executive producer role is outdated and provisional.
